Jensen Huang called Marvell “the next trillion-dollar company.” Looking at the numbers, that case is hard to make. Marvell is worth about $168B today. A $1T valuation means roughly $1,100 per share—around 6x from here. The company’s own target is $16.5B in revenue by FY2028. A $1T valuation would be about 60x sales. That’s a multiple you might see for a licensing business like Arm, not a chip designer. The earnings math is even tougher. Marvell targets an operating margin in the high end of the 38–40% range by FY2028. If achieved, that’s roughly $6.6B operating income and about $5.5B net income after interest and taxes. A $1T valuation would imply roughly 180x earnings—and that’s using adjusted numbers. On a GAAP basis, the picture is very different. In Q1 FY2027, Marvell generated $2.42B in revenue but only $34.5M in net income. Adjusted net income was $718M, with most of the gap coming from stock-based compensation and acquisition-related amortization. Here’s the key point: to justify a $1T valuation at a more typical 30x P/E, Marvell would need about $33B in net income. At a 35% net margin, that implies roughly $95B in revenue. Marvell’s own investor presentation estimates the entire 2028 data center market at $94B. In other words, it would have to capture essentially the whole market. There’s also dilution to consider: investments in Celestial AI and XConn, Nvidia’s investment, and the $2B preferred stock issuance. As market cap grows, per-share value doesn’t necessarily keep pace. The stock has already fallen from $329 to $187, showing just how fragile the narrative can be. Marvell is a strong company, and its growth is real. But $1 trillion isn’t a valuation—it’s a slogan. Source: Marvell Q1 FY2027 earnings and the company’s investor presentation. Note: The bull case also deserves attention. With 45% revenue growth in custom silicon and interconnect while operating expenses grow only in the high teens, the company could see significant operating leverage. $MRVL

Hyperscaler cloud backlogs have exploded. Q2 2025 → Q2 2026: • Microsoft: $368B → $678B (+84%) • Oracle: $138B → $638B (+362%) • Google: $106B → $514B (+385%) • Amazon: $195B → $496B (+154%) Total contracted demand: ~$2.3 trillion. AI demand is vastly outpacing available capacity. Oracle and Google, in particular, are seeing explosive growth.

$BE is one of the holdings in my portfolio, so I’ve been watching it closely. The chart is showing a very interesting setup. Q2 was a blowout: $1.07B in revenue (+165% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.78—both well ahead of expectations. Yet the stock fell from $351 to around $205. The selloff wasn’t driven by earnings. Confidence took a hit after Hunterbrook’s short report, followed by price target cuts from Wells Fargo ($176) and Jefferies ($188). Technically: • A bearish order block formed at the top, followed by a break in market structure. • The stock has bounced from the lows, but RSI is still below 50. • OBV hasn’t recovered, meaning buying volume isn’t confirming the rebound. The most important detail is the volume profile. The high-volume node sits between $75 and $130, while the area above it is relatively thin. The current price is trading in that low-volume zone, which means there isn’t much structural support underneath. Until $240 is reclaimed, I view this as a relief rally rather than a confirmed trend reversal.
I opened my largest position at the close two days ago. $AAOI

Bloomberg: Moonshot gained access to approximately 20,000 $NVDA chips through Alibaba, according to sources, which say the chips were H200s. Alibaba denied providing H200 compute, but it did not deny the claim that Moonshot accessed 20,000 chips. There is also reportedly a Blackwell supply channel through Southeast Asia (via Thailand), which may have been used for Kimi K3. Despite U.S. export controls, China’s AI development continues to advance. #NVDA

Reddit $RDDT posted a strong Q2: Revenue reached $805M (+61%), while advertising revenue grew 64%. However, CEO Steve Huffman said Google search referrals have become “choppy” and volatile, reducing visibility. “AI Overviews haven’t created the same value as the traditional 10 blue links.” The company is focusing on becoming a daily destination for users rather than relying on drive-by search traffic. The stock fell 11% in after-hours trading, highlighting that the AI search risk is real. #RDDT #AI
